source_observations.observation: Two means paired with two affixes in order. Each permits both given and done. The indeclinable expresses the instrumental relation without an overt instrumental.
Enhancement by an instrument. Earrings and clothes select ṭhañ, work and costume select yat.
Dative relation and a list for capability. Yoga separately admits both yat and ṭhañ.
Ukañ on karman, the object denoted being specifically a bow.

source_observations.locator: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa 4.12.1, grammar and Sanskrit verse
source_observations.observation: Kārmukam as the grammatical object of jagrāha in the Sugrīva episode.
Nominative support, a genitive relation to the recipient of the arrived time. The season, and two named supplements, have independent examples.
In the Vedic domain ghas supersedes the aṇ of 105. Pada designation before ghas blocks bhāṅga guṇa under 6.4.146.
Ṛtviyaḥ agrees with yoniḥ. Sāyaṇa explains its seasonal occurrence and identifies the fire stick.
Same seasonal adjective in the corresponding opening. The second line has ā roha and rayim.
Names the ritual portion in a relative identification after the Bṛhaspati narrative.
Explicit arrived-eater expansion, followed in this edition by the agnipada supplement citation assigned to 5.1.97.
Prāśitram is the direct object of the verb for eating the portion.

source_observations.locator: TS 2.6.8, Pūṣan narrative, Padapāṭha and Sāyaṇa
source_observations.observation: Different adjective aprāśitriyaḥ of the participant, with a gloss of ineligibility. The commentary also has the genitive of the portion.
Contrast due time with an extended period. Long-standing debt and enmity take the same written adjective.

source_observations.observation: Kālikā qualifies the interest accruing monthly.

source_observations.locator: Nārada, monthly interest, cross-edition numbering in Payer
source_observations.observation: The pair of definitions is numbered 88–89, Jolly 103–104. The term applies to frequency of interest.

source_observations.locator: Manu 8.153 with Medhātithi and Jha's notes
source_observations.observation: The verse has the compound atisāṃvatsarīm after external sandhi, and kālavṛddhiḥ rather than the feminine simple kālikā. Compare the cited Nārada gloss.
